recipes.name: Molasses Brined Pork Chops
ingredients_raw: 4 (2 1/4 inch thick) center cut, bone-in pork chops

steps.text: Combine boiling water, salt, molasses, and cloves in a large container, stirring until salt and molasses are dissolved. Cool to room temperature.
Stir cold water into molasses brine to combine.
Submerge pork chops completely in molasses brine. Cover container and refrigerate for 6 hours.
Remove pork chops from brine; pat dry with paper towels. Lightly oil each chop. Discard brine.
Preheat an outdoor grill for medium-high heat and lightly oil the grate.

Cook pork chops on the hottest part of the preheated grill until both sides of each chop is browned, 2 to 3 minutes. Transfer chops to the medium-high part of the grill; cook until slightly pink in centers, 6 to 8 minutes per side. An instant-read thermometer inserted into centers should read 145 degrees F (63 degrees C).

raw_recipe.headline: Molasses Brined Pork Chops
raw_recipe.description: Chef John's molasses-brined pork chops recipe begins with a brine made with salt, molasses, and cloves, elevating your chops to new levels of succulence.

review.reviewBody: I did this two ways -- one with a short brine (because I couldn't wait another day) and one with an overnight brine. Definitely worth the wait! The chops were juicy and delicious!

Whenever I tell my husband we're having pork chops for dinner, I see his shoulders sag. The pork chops he envisions are those of his childhood: chops you could pound nails with! What a pleasure to eat these chops, so moist. I followed the written recipe and also jaccarded the chops before putting them in the brine. Rather than grilling (14 degrees outside), I used my trusty cast iron pan. Next time I make these for dinner I'll increase the cloves and include a bit of liquid smoke.

Made half recipe of brine. Used four loin chops, each one-inch thick (two pounds). Chops two and a half inches thick would be a small roast to me! Used 7 X 11 Pyrex to brine; chops just fit. Have half of the brine left over. (I poured the brine over the chops; when the pan was full I had half the brine left over...about two cups. The brine I saved did not come into contact with the pork.) Poked each chop four times with a fork. Did not use cloves. Cooked chops on the stovetop using a meat thermometer. Still I overcooked them a bit. They were much better than the pork chops I usually make! I would use this recipe again.

I too thought this was too salty ( and I love salt!), but it still gets five stars! I brined for six hours and it was delicious and juicy. I will brine even longer next time. I also really love the flavor of cloves so I added twice the whole cloves plus 1/4 teaspoon of powdered cloves to the brine. I grilled the chops a little too long, but they were still very juicy and flavorful. I am not a fan of vinegar so the Carolina bbq sauce was not for me, but my husband loved it. This recipe is a keeper!

I actually made this twice. I saw someone's review where they marinated for 2 days and it was very good and not salty. I had some boneless sirloin chops that were very thick that I bought on sale. We had cooked some on the grill first without marinating them and they were very tough. I knew I had to find something since I had bought 30 lbs (They were .99 lb sale). I marinated the first batch 6 or 8 hours and they were good. More tender, but delicious and did not taste overly salty to us and we use very little salt here. I, at the same time, marinated some for 2 days like the reviewer I read. OMG, so much better. Super tender and juicy. Could practically cut with a fork. Not salty at all. Even leftovers right out of the refridge were tender and still juicy. This is my go to marinade for pork to be grilled now. We used no other sauce or spices. Love it!

Edit - I forgot. I did not use cloves. I did not have any, but I did add sage leaves, which gave it a subtle, but good flavor. I did not measure, I just dropped some in.

I made this with a ten oz. pork tenderloin. I only made half the brine, and next time I will halve it again. I kept it in the fridge overnight, and then, turning it once, cooked it in my gas BBQ at 400 degrees until the center read 145 degrees (about sixteen minutes).
It was pretty good, nice and tender with an even brown color, but I hardly (if at all) tasted any molasses, clove or garlic flavor, Maybe I will cut down the water still more next time.

I made half of the recipe except 3 whole cloves and 1/8 Cup of the salt. I rinsed off the meat and then patted it dry. To test the brine I didn't use any additional BBQ sauce just grilled them as is. They were fabulous!

Great for thick chops that tend to get tough. I cut the brine in half for 6 pork chops, and it was perfect, marinated about 18 hours. They were so tasty we didn't even need to baste them with barbecue sauce on the grill, just served it on the side.
Tasty but too salty. I cut the brining recipe in half because I had 4 3/4" chops. Next time I would either decrease the salt or rinse the chops before grilling. Tender and juicy.

We thought it was excellent. We used 2 thick & 2 regular chops. We brined them with extra cloves overnight & they turned out great. Watching the temperature I think made a lot of difference on the grill. Thanks Chef John.

last weeks dinner was a hit! only modification was clove powder vs cloves 
.(is what I had on hand) 

I made this with thin and 1.5 inch chops and only brined for 5.5hrs. Obviously I cooked the small one less time.....anywho totally delish, juicy, all kids 2, 4, and 12 gobbled it up and we will be doing this again and hopefully I will get longer time to brine.

The brine does a great job of keeping the chops juicy. I even overcooked them and they were still juicy. I did cut back on the salt a bit, but otherwise made as directed. I served with just a light touch of the Carolina-Style Barbeque Sauce listed in the Editor's Notes. Very good meal overall.

I've made this multiple times and have not needed to change a thing. Although the second time I made it I inadvertently used table salt instead of kosher (larger grains). Needless to say that was a mistake I never repeated. Way too salty! But follow the recipe and it will be delicious! :-)
I halfed the recipe for 2 large pork chops, used 1/4 tsp powdered cloves, plus added 1 tsp garlic pork chops turned out tender and full of flavour
This recipe was terrible. I made it exactly as written without any changes. The cloves and salt are overpowering.
It was awesome. While i did not get for make Chef John's Carolina Style BBQ sauce, it was perfect. And I just stuck to the recipe

My go to brine . Results in juicy and tender pork chops. Watch the temperature not the time and shoot for 145 degrees. In my case, they hit 145 much sooner than the suggested cooking time. I found that using a few shakes of ground cloves spice works well versus actual cloves.
Made these pork chops. I baked them instead of grilled. Came out great.
The pork chops were juicy but needed some extra flavor which is probably why chef John adds bbq sauce. It was good but not great. Pork chops were brined for 48 hours

Very tasty and juicy. I did use a mustard based Carolina BBQ sauce part way through grilling and I think that took it to another level! Will make again for sure. 
Paired with grilled veggies
